vocab.en: you (polite: to an older person or someone you have just met)
to be called (a name); to call someone
to meet, get to know; to know (a person)
to be free, to have time
sentence particle: friendly surprise or a soft check (英文老師喔！)
sentence particle: a warm, casual push (來我家吃飯啦！)

grammar.note_en: 是 links a person to a nationality, a job or a relation: 我是美國人, 我是英文老師, 這是我兒子. Its negative is 不是, and it never changes for person or tense.
Family members and your own home take no 的 after the pronoun: 我先生, 我兒子, 我爸爸、媽媽, 我家, 你家. Keep 的 for ordinary things you own (我的手機).
林太太 and 小明 turn statements into yes/no questions with 嗎 at the end: 你是新來的嗎？ 你來屏東工作嗎？ 你有哥哥姊姊嗎？ The word order does not change. 大衛 answers the first two with 對 'right'.

pronunciation.note_en: ㄣ vs ㄥ: 林 ㄌㄧㄣˊ, 您 ㄋㄧㄣˊ, 認識 ㄖㄣˋ and 人 ㄖㄣˊ close with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth; 姓 ㄒㄧㄥˋ, 英文 ㄧㄥ, 高興 ㄒㄧㄥˋ, 屏東 ㄆㄧㄥˊ and 小明 ㄇㄧㄥˊ close with the back of the tongue. 姓林 puts the two side by side. Many people in Taiwan merge ㄧㄥ into ㄧㄣ in casual speech: understand it, but keep them apart yourself. Tone pair 3+3: 你好 is said ㄋㄧˊ ㄏㄠˇ, and 可以 and 我有 change the same way; the Zhuyin keeps the base tones.

speaking.prompt_en: You meet a new neighbour in Pingtung. Greet them, say your name and where you are from, say what you do, and tell them about your family. Ask them one question with 嗎, then say goodbye.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你在屏東認識了一位新鄰居。請你說你叫什麼名字、是哪國人、做什麼工作，也說一說你的家人。用「嗎」問一個問題，再說再見。
checklist_en: greeted with 你好 or 您好 and ended with 再見
gave my name with 我叫… (or my surname with 我姓…)
used 是 for where I am from or my job (我是美國人, 我是…)
named family members without 的 (我爸爸, 我哥哥)
asked a yes/no question ending in 嗎
said 你好 as ㄋㄧˊ ㄏㄠˇ and kept ㄧㄥ in 姓 / 英文 apart from ㄧㄣ in 林 / 您

writing.prompt_en: Write a short self-introduction for a new neighbour (4 to 6 sentences): your name, where you are from, your job and your family.
writing.prompt_zh: 請寫一段自我介紹：你叫什麼名字、是哪國人、做什麼工作，還有你的家人。

units.culture_en: 林太太 says 我先生姓林 'my husband's surname is Lin': 太太 'Mrs' goes after the husband's surname, while women in Taiwan normally keep their own surname after marriage, so she may well have a different surname herself. Children address adults they know as 叔叔 'uncle' or 阿姨 'auntie', and a teacher as 老師, not by name; that is why 小明 greets 大衛 with 老師好！ In everyday Taiwan speech 和 'and' is often said ㄏㄢˋ, which MOE lists as a colloquial reading (語音); the app teaches ㄏㄜˊ.

units.can_do_en: I can buy a drink and a snack at a convenience store, point to what I want, answer the cashier's usual questions (hot or iced, a bag) and pay.

vocab.en: Welcome! (what shop staff say when you walk in; 謝謝光臨 when you leave)
to want; would like (when ordering or buying)
cup, glass (measure word for drinks; 大杯 'a large one')
general measure word (often said lightly: 這個, 兩個)
ice; iced, cold (冰的 'an iced one')
or (in a question that offers a choice)
dollar (spoken; prices are written with 元)
to give change (找你五十五塊 'here's 55 change'); to look for
friendly sentence-final particle that makes a remark warmer (很好吃喔！)

grammar.note_en: Pointing at things on the shelf: 這個麵包 'this bun' needs the measure word 個 between 這 and the noun, and 這個嗎？ 'this one?' uses 這個 alone. 這是你的發票 shows 這 on its own as the subject.
Every item you buy is counted with a number and a measure word: 一瓶水, 一杯咖啡, 兩個 (麵包). 'Two' before a measure word is 兩, never 二.

pronunciation.note_en: Puff or no puff: 杯 ㄅㄟ, 包 ㄅㄠ and 個 ㄍㄜˋ have no burst of air; 瓶 ㄆㄧㄥˊ, 票 ㄆㄧㄠˋ, 咖 ㄎㄚ and 塊 ㄎㄨㄞˋ have a strong one. Tone pair 1+4 in 發票 and 商店: hold the first syllable high and level, then fall from the top. Listen for sandhi too: 一瓶, 一杯 and 一百 are said ㄧˋ, 一共 is said ㄧˊ, 不要 is said ㄅㄨˊ ㄧㄠˋ, and 你好 and 我買 start with a rising ㄋㄧˊ / ㄨㄛˊ.

speaking.prompt_en: You are at the counter of a convenience store in Pingtung. Ask for one drink and one snack, answer the cashier's questions (hot or iced? a bag?), then pay and take your change.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你在便利商店買東西。說你要什麼，回答店員的問題，然後付錢。
checklist_en: used 要 + number + measure word + noun (一瓶水, 一個麵包)
used 兩, not 二, for 'two' before a measure word
pointed at something with 這個 or 那個
answered 熱的還是冰的？ with 熱的 or 冰的
answered 要不要袋子？ with 要 or 不要, plus 謝謝
said the price with 塊 (一百四十五塊)

writing.prompt_en: Write three short sentences: what you buy at the convenience store (with measure words), whether you want a bag, and how much it costs altogether.
writing.prompt_zh: 寫三個句子：你在便利商店買什麼？要不要袋子？一共多少錢？
writing.model_zh: 我去便利商店，買一瓶水和兩個麵包。我不要袋子。一共九十五塊。
writing.model_zhuyin: ㄨㄛˇ ㄑㄩˋ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ㄌㄧˋ ㄕㄤ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄇㄞˇ ㄧ ㄆㄧㄥˊ ㄕㄨㄟˇ ㄏㄜˊ ㄌㄧㄤˇ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄇㄧㄢˋ ㄅㄠ ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄉㄞˋ ˙ㄗ ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ ㄐㄧㄡˇ ㄕˊ ㄨˇ ㄎㄨㄞˋ

units.culture_en: Staff greet you with 歡迎光臨 when you come in and say 謝謝光臨 when you leave; you don't need to answer. Convenience stores in Taiwan may not give out free plastic shopping bags, so the cashier asks whether you want one and charges a small fee; many people bring their own. The receipt (統一發票) is also a lottery ticket, with winning numbers drawn every two months, so people keep it; the cashier may instead ask about a 載具, a phone barcode that saves the receipt electronically.

units.can_do_en: I can order food and drinks for two at a breakfast shop, ask whether something is good, and answer 'for here or to go?'

dialogue.speaker: 老闆娘

dialogue.speaker: 志明

dialogue.en: For here.
dialogue.spoken: ㄋㄟˋ ㄩㄥˋ

dialogue.speaker: 老闆娘
dialogue.zh: 一共一百二十五塊。你們先坐，好了我拿給你們。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ ㄧ ㄅㄞˇ ㄦˋ ㄕˊ ㄨˇ ㄎㄨㄞˋ ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄒㄧㄢ ㄗㄨㄛˋ ㄏㄠˇ ˙ㄌㄜ ㄨㄛˇ ㄋㄚˊ ㄍㄟˇ ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄇㄣ

dialogue.speaker: 志明

dialogue.spoken: ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄨㄛˊ ㄑㄧㄥˊ ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄌㄚ

dialogue.speaker: 安娜

dialogue.speaker: 老闆娘

grammar.note_en: Every order is number + measure word + food: 一個蛋餅, 一份蘿蔔糕, 兩杯冰奶茶. Drinks take 杯, a portion takes 份, and 'two' before a measure word is 兩, not 二.
Anna asks for an opinion with 好不好吃？ (the two-syllable 好吃 repeats only 好), and the owner offers an extra with 要不要加蛋？. Neither question takes 嗎.

pronunciation.note_en: Three aspirated sounds meet at breakfast: ㄘ in 早餐 (tongue behind the teeth, like 'ts' with a puff), ㄔ in 吃, 奶茶 and 常常 (tongue tip up behind the gum ridge), ㄑ in 請 (tongue tip down, lips spread). Tone pair 3+1: in 早餐 and 早安 the third tone stays low (21) with no rise before the high, level first tone.

units.culture_en: Taiwan's 早餐店 (breakfast shops) open early and sell both Chinese-style items such as 蛋餅 and 蘿蔔糕 and Western-style ones such as 漢堡 (hamburgers) and 吐司 (toast), usually with 奶茶 or 紅茶. At many shops you tick your order on a paper menu, or just say it at the counter. Staff often call customers 帥哥 ('handsome') or 美女 ('beautiful') whatever their age; it is simply friendly. Regulars shorten 大杯冰奶茶 to 大冰奶.

units.can_do_en: I can order a drink at a drink stand, choose the size, the sugar level and the ice, and ask a friend if they want one too.

grammar.note_en: Drinks are counted with the measure word 杯: 一杯珍珠奶茶, 一杯熱紅茶. The same 杯 names the size, 大杯 and 中杯.
小美 asks her friend 你要不要喝？ and 阿明 asks the clerk 你們有沒有熱的？ The verb said twice with 不 or 沒 in the middle makes the question, so 嗎 is not added.
The clerk gives the total as 九十五塊: 九十 (nine tens) + 五. Prices are said with 塊 in speech.

pronunciation.note_en: 半糖 puts ㄢ and ㄤ side by side: 半 ㄅㄢˋ ends with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth, and 糖 ㄊㄤˊ ends with the back of the tongue raised and a darker a. 甜 ㄊㄧㄢˊ is different again: ㄧㄢ sounds like "yen", not "yahn". For the tone pair, 紅茶 and 無糖 are two rising tones in a row (2+2); let both rise. Also listen for 一 in 一杯, said ㄧˋ before the first tone of 杯.

units.culture_en: At Taiwan's hand-shaken drink shops (手搖飲) the clerk asks for the sugar level and the ice level separately, and the usual answer gives the sugar first: 半糖少冰. Common sugar levels are 全糖 (full), 少糖 (less), 半糖 (half), 微糖 (a little) and 無糖 (none). Common ice levels are 正常冰 (regular), 少冰 (less), 微冰 (a little) and 去冰 (no ice in the cup), and some drinks can be made 熱 (hot). The exact amounts differ from shop to shop. Bubble milk tea, 珍珠奶茶, is usually shortened to 珍奶.

grammar.note_en: Time phrases go from big to small and sit before the verb: 我十一點有中文課, 禮拜六晚上六點半，火車站見. In speech the date is 號 (十四號), and 半 means half past (十二點半).
Clock times and dates are built place by place, so the order changes the number: 十四 'ten four' is 14 (十四號) but 四十 'four ten' is 40 (十點四十分). 十一 and 十二 work the same way.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep 十 ㄕˊ and 四 ㄙˋ apart: for ㄕ the tongue tip is up just behind the gum ridge, ㄙ is a plain s, and neither has an 'ee' sound (the empty rhyme). The tones differ too, so 十四 ㄕˊ ㄙˋ (14) and 四十 ㄙˋ ㄕˊ (40) sound clearly different. 星 ㄒㄧㄥ in 星期 is the third sound: tongue tip down, lips spread. 幾點 is a 3+3 pair, so 幾 is said rising (like ㄐㄧˊ ㄉㄧㄢˇ) though it is written ㄐㄧˇ.

units.culture_en: 星期 and 禮拜 both name the days of the week (星期六 = 禮拜六 = Saturday). In everyday Taiwan speech you will hear 禮拜 a lot, while written schedules and opening hours often use 星期 or the short form 週 (週六). People tell the time on a 12-hour clock with 早上, 下午 or 晚上 in front (晚上六點半), but train timetables, like the ones at Pingtung station, use the 24-hour clock: 晚上六點半 is 18:30.

vocab.en: boss, owner; what you call a stall owner
order, portion (measure word for a serving of food)
to give (change); also: to look for

grammar.note_en: Prices use the full number system with 塊 after the number: 六十塊, 二十五塊, 一百七十塊, 八百三十塊, 一千塊. Say the 一 in 一百 and 一千.
Every order is number + measure word + noun: 一份臭豆腐, 兩份, 兩杯紅茶. Use 兩 (not 二) before a measure word; 份 counts servings of food and 杯 counts drinks.
When the food comes out, the owner asks 誰要辣的？ 'Who is having the spicy one?' 誰 sits where the answer goes, so 阿芳 just puts 我 in its place: 我要辣的。

pronunciation.note_en: Prices and food mix all three: ㄑ in 錢, 千 and 七 (tongue tip down, lips spread), ㄔ in 吃, 臭 and 茶 (tongue tip up), ㄘ in 不錯 (a flat 'ts' with a puff). 老闆, 可以, 只有 and 找你 are written 3+3 but said 2+3 (老闆 sounds like ㄌㄠˊ ㄅㄢˇ).

comprehension.question_en: How much is one order of stinky tofu?
How do they want their two orders?
What do they order to drink?
Mark pays with a NT$1,000 bill. How much change does he get?
Who gets the spicy stinky tofu?

speaking.prompt_en: Role-play at a night-market stall with a friend: ask the price of a snack and a drink, order with a number + measure word, say how spicy each order should be, ask for the total, say what bill you are paying with, and sort out whose order is whose when the food comes.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你和朋友在夜市買吃的。問老闆一份多少錢、一杯多少錢，說你們要幾份、要不要辣，再問一共多少錢。
checklist_en: asked a price with a measure word (一份／一杯…多少錢？)
ordered with number + measure word, using 兩 before the measure word (兩份, 兩杯)
said a price over 100 correctly (一百七十塊, 八百三十塊)
asked 一共多少錢？ and understood the change (找你…塊)
asked or answered a 誰 question (誰要辣的？ 我要辣的。)

writing.prompt_en: You're going to the night market tonight. Write 3–4 sentences: what you will buy, how many (number + measure word), what each costs and the total.
writing.prompt_zh: 今天晚上你要去夜市。你要買什麼？要幾份、幾杯？一份多少錢？一共多少錢？

units.culture_en: Prices on signs are written with 元 or a $ sign (New Taiwan dollars), but people say 塊 out loud: 六十元 on the sign is 六十塊. Food prices at night-market stalls are fixed, so you don't bargain for food. You call out 老闆 to get a stall owner's attention (老闆娘 if a woman runs the stall). Many stalls still take mainly cash, so coins and NT$100 bills are handy; if you pay with a NT$1,000 bill, the owner gives you change (找錢). Fried 臭豆腐 is usually served with 台式泡菜, a sweet-and-sour pickled cabbage.

units.can_do_en: I can ask where a street or place is, follow simple directions (straight on, turn at the second corner, on the left or right) and repeat them back.

grammar.note_en: 大衛 asks 中正路在哪裡？ and 阿姨 asks back 你要去中正路哪裡？: 哪裡 sits where the place will be in the answer, and neither question takes 嗎.
Every location answer is 在 + place with no 是: 三十八號就在郵局旁邊, 在郵局左邊還是右邊？, 在右邊.
大衛 gives the address big to small, road first and the number with 號 last: 在中正路三十八號.

pronunciation.note_en: Directions are full of ㄐ / ㄓ / ㄗ: 就 ㄐㄧㄡˋ and 家 ㄐㄧㄚ (tongue flat, lips spread), 中正路 ㄓㄨㄥ ㄓㄥˋ and 這裡 ㄓㄜˋ (tongue tip curled back), 走 ㄗㄡˇ, 在 ㄗㄞˋ and 左 ㄗㄨㄛˇ (tongue tip behind the teeth). Many Taiwan speakers say ㄓ close to ㄗ, so 中正 may sound like zong-zeng; understand it, but say ㄓ yourself. Tone pair 3+4 in 走路, 請問, 我要, 你會: keep the third tone low (21) with no rise, then drop from high for the fourth.

units.culture_en: In Taiwan, 不會 or 不會啦 ('not at all') is a very common reply to 謝謝, used alongside 不客氣. 阿姨 'auntie' is a friendly, polite way to address a woman about your parents' age, even a stranger. Most towns in Taiwan have a 中正路 and a 中山路, named after Chiang Kai-shek (蔣中正) and Sun Yat-sen (孫中山), so when you give an address, say which town it is in.

vocab.en: there; (你們那裡) where you are from
auntie (an older woman, e.g. a neighbour)

grammar.note_en: 陳阿姨 asks 你們那裡冬天冷不冷？ and Mark asks 雨會不會很大？: an adjective or 會 said twice, positive then negative, makes a yes/no question with no 嗎. 會不會 + adjective is the usual Taiwan way to ask about the weather or how someone feels.
陳伯伯 says 屏東冬天不冷，也不常下雨: 不 goes straight before an adjective (不冷) or before an adverb and verb (不常下雨) to talk about how things usually are.

pronunciation.note_en: 下雨 ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄩˇ 'to rain' and 下午 ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄨˇ 'afternoon' are both T4 + T3 and differ only in ㄩ and ㄨ: for ㄩ say ㄧ (as in 阿姨) and round your lips without moving your tongue back. Keep the T3 of 雨 and 午 low (21) inside a sentence; a rise is allowed only at the end of a phrase.

speaking.prompt_en: You meet a neighbour at your door in the morning. Greet them, say what the weather is like today, ask whether it will rain this afternoon, and say where you are going.
speaking.prompt_zh: 早上你在門口看到鄰居。跟他說早，說說今天的天氣，問問下午會不會下雨，也說你要去哪裡。
checklist_en: greeted with 早 and a title (阿姨早！ / 伯伯早！)
described the weather with 好 / 很 / 非常 + 熱 or 冷
asked an A-not-A question with no 嗎 (會不會下雨？ 熱不熱？)
used 不 before an adjective (不冷, 不熱)
said 下雨 with ㄩ, clearly different from 下午

units.culture_en: Older people in Taiwan often greet you with 吃飽了嗎？ 'Have you eaten?'. It is a greeting, not an invitation: just answer 吃飽了 or 還沒. Neighbours and other older adults are called 阿姨 'auntie' and 伯伯 'uncle' even when they are not relatives, often with their surname: 陳阿姨. Pingtung is in the far south of Taiwan: summers are hot, with frequent heavy afternoon showers, and winters are mild and mostly dry.

units.can_do_en: I can order a bento for here or to go, ask for an extra item, say how the food is, and ask the owner to pack up what I can't finish.

vocab.en: boxed meal, bento (rice with a main dish and sides)
measure word for small round things (eggs, candies)
to trouble (someone); 麻煩 + request = 'could you please...'
to wrap; 包起來 = pack up (leftovers, a gift)
to finish; verb + 完 = finish doing it (吃不完 = can't finish eating)
time, occurrence; 下次 = next time

grammar.note_en: 內用還是外帶？ is the first question at any 便當店: 還是 joins the two choices, so the question needs no 嗎. 小美 uses it again: 雞腿便當還是排骨便當？
又便宜又好吃 and 又大又香 put two good qualities of the food side by side. Each 又 goes right before its adjective, with no 很.
幫 + person + verb asks someone to do something for you: 麻煩幫我加一顆滷蛋, 可以幫我包起來嗎？ The owner answers with the same pattern: 我幫你包起來。

pronunciation.note_en: ㄐ, ㄓ and ㄗ all come up here: 雞 ㄐㄧ, 炸 ㄓㄚˊ, 自己 ㄗˋ ㄐㄧˇ, 在 ㄗㄞˋ. In relaxed Taiwan speech ㄓ often drifts toward ㄗ (炸 can sound like ㄗㄚˊ): understand both, but say ㄓ with the tongue tip curled back. Tone pair 3+3: 老闆 ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ and 小美 ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄇㄟˇ are said 2+3, the same shape as 排骨 ㄆㄞˊ ㄍㄨˇ.

units.culture_en: 便當 comes from the Japanese word bentō and is Taiwan's everyday boxed meal: rice with one main dish, such as a fried chicken leg (雞腿) or a pork chop (排骨), and a few side dishes. Shops ask 內用還是外帶 ('for here or to go?'), and you call the person running a small shop 老闆 (a woman who runs it is often called 老闆娘). 不錯吃 ('pretty tasty') and 有 + verb (你有吃飽嗎？) are everyday Taiwan Mandarin.

units.can_do_en: I can choose between scooter, train and intercity bus, ask how long a trip takes and how far a place is, and ask station staff about the next train.

grammar.note_en: 從屏東到高雄 marks where the trip starts and ends; the question about the trip (坐火車要多久？) follows it.
騎機車比坐火車慢 compares two ways of getting there: A 比 B + adjective, with no 很 before the adjective.
車站離我家不遠 says how far one place is from another: A 離 B + 遠 / 近 (negated with 不).

pronunciation.note_en: 騎機車 ㄑㄧˊ ㄐㄧ ㄔㄜ puts ㄑ and ㄔ side by side: for 騎 the tongue tip is down behind the lower teeth with the lips spread; for 車 the tip is up just behind the gum ridge. Both have a strong puff of air, and so does 從 ㄘㄨㄥˊ ("ts" plus a puff). In 火車 and 我家 (3 + 1), keep the third tone low (21) with no rise before the high, level first tone.

units.culture_en: Taiwan calls a scooter 機車 (the Mainland word is 摩托車), and in Pingtung it is the everyday way to get around. By law the rider and the passenger must both wear a helmet (安全帽). At many big intersections scooters may not turn left directly: they make a two-stage left turn (兩段式左轉), going straight first, waiting in the marked box, then crossing with the next green light. When you ride Taiwan Railway trains without a reserved seat, you can tap in and out with an EasyCard (悠遊卡) or an iPASS (一卡通, the card from Kaohsiung that is common in the south) instead of buying a ticket. Kenting has no railway, so people get there by intercity bus or by road.

grammar.note_en: The doctor opens with 怎麼了？哪裡不舒服？, the everyday way to ask what's wrong. A friend who sees you looking ill would say 你怎麼了？
痛了兩天了: the length of time goes after the verb, and the final 了 says it is still going on. It answers the doctor's 痛多久了？
The doctor says the throat is 有點紅, and Mark softens his symptom with 有一點發燒: 'a bit', for something unwelcome.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep three sounds apart: ㄒ in 休息 ㄒㄧㄡ ㄒㄧˊ (tongue tip down, lips spread), ㄕ in 發燒 ㄈㄚ ㄕㄠ and 舒服 ㄕㄨ ˙ㄈㄨ (tongue tip up behind the gum ridge), and ㄙ in 咳嗽 ㄎㄜˊ ㄙㄡˋ and 三次 ㄙㄢ ㄘˋ (a plain s). Many Taiwan speakers say ㄕ close to ㄙ; understand it, but produce ㄕ. Tone pair 2+4 (rise, then a high fall): 咳嗽, 嚴重. 一共 is written ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ but said ㄧˊ ㄍㄨㄥˋ, the same 2+4 shape, and 不要 is said ㄅㄨˊ ㄧㄠˋ.

units.culture_en: Taiwan's National Health Insurance (全民健保) covers almost everyone who lives here, and each insured person has an IC card with a photo, the 健保卡. Hand it in at the counter every time you see a doctor: the clinic registers you (掛號), and you pay a registration fee (掛號費) set by the clinic plus a fixed copayment (部分負擔). Many neighbourhood clinics give you a number and show the number now being seen on a display, and they often hand you the medicine right there, in a bag that tells you how many times a day to take it and whether before or after meals (飯前 / 飯後). Foreign residents with a residence permit (ARC) can join after six months in Taiwan; people employed in Taiwan join from their first day of work.

units.can_do_en: I can tell a pharmacist what's wrong and since when, understand how often and how much medicine to take, and ask what to do if it doesn't get better.

dialogue.zh: 好。如果明天還是一直拉肚子，怎麼辦？
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄏㄠˇ ㄖㄨˊ ㄍㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄏㄞˊ ㄕˋ ㄧ ㄓˊ ㄌㄚ ㄉㄨˋ ˙ㄗ ㄗㄣˇ ˙ㄇㄜ ㄅㄢˋ

dialogue.zh: 那就要去看醫生喔。這盒藥一百二，藥膏一百八，一共三百。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄋㄚˋ ㄐㄧㄡˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄑㄩˋ ㄎㄢˋ ㄧ ㄕㄥ ㄛ ㄓㄜˋ ㄏㄜˊ ㄧㄠˋ ㄧ ㄅㄞˇ ㄦˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄍㄠ ㄧ ㄅㄞˇ ㄅㄚ ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ ㄙㄢ ㄅㄞˇ

bad, broken; 吃壞肚子 to get an upset stomach from something you ate

grammar.note_en: The pharmacist says 洗了澡就擦一點: put the cream on right after your shower. 了 goes straight after the first verb (洗了澡) and 就 straight before the second; the writing model does the same with 吃了飯就吃一顆.
吃東西要小心一點: an adjective + 一點 asks for 'a bit more' of that quality, here 'be a bit more careful about what you eat'. Don't mix it up with 有一點 before an adjective, which means 'somewhat' (unit L2-03).
Anna states the problem first and puts 怎麼辦 at the end: 如果明天還是一直拉肚子，怎麼辦？ 'If I still have diarrhea tomorrow, what should I do?'

pronunciation.note_en: Aspiration: ㄉ in 肚子 ㄉㄨˋ ˙ㄗ has no puff of air, ㄊ in 條 ㄊㄧㄠˊ and 一天 ㄧ ㄊㄧㄢ has a strong one (肚子 / 兔子 ㄊㄨˋ ˙ㄗ is a classic pair). In the same way, ㄍ in 藥膏 ㄧㄠˋ ㄍㄠ has no puff and ㄎ in 一顆 ㄧ ㄎㄜ has one; ㄗ in 洗澡 ㄒㄧˇ ㄗㄠˇ has none and ㄘ in 擦 ㄘㄚ and 三次 ㄙㄢ ㄘˋ has one. Tone pair 4+1 (a high fall, then high and level): 藥師 ㄧㄠˋ ㄕ, 藥膏 ㄧㄠˋ ㄍㄠ; jump back up for the second syllable instead of letting it fall too. Sandhi: 一次一顆 is said ㄧˊ ㄘˋ ㄧˋ ㄎㄜ, 不要 ㄅㄨˊ ㄧㄠˋ, 一共 ㄧˊ ㄍㄨㄥˋ, and the word 洗澡 on its own ㄒㄧˊ ㄗㄠˇ (3+3).

speaking.prompt_en: You're at a pharmacy in Pingtung. Tell the pharmacist what's wrong and since when, answer whether you have a fever, ask how to take the medicine, and ask what to do if you're not better tomorrow.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你在藥局。請跟藥師說你哪裡不舒服、從什麼時候開始的、有沒有發燒，然後問藥怎麼吃，還有如果明天還是不舒服，怎麼辦。
checklist_en: said what's wrong (我肚子不太舒服 / 一直拉肚子)
said since when with 從……開始
asked how often and how much (一天吃幾次？一次幾顆？)
asked 如果……，怎麼辦？
kept unaspirated ㄉ (肚子) and aspirated ㄊ (一天) apart

writing.prompt_en: You went to a pharmacy today. Write a short LINE message (3–5 sentences) to a friend: what was wrong, what the pharmacist said, and how you take the medicine. Try 了……就…… and 小心一點.

units.culture_en: Neighbourhood pharmacies (社區藥局) in Taiwan are run by licensed pharmacists (藥師), and for a small problem like an upset stomach or mosquito bites you can describe it at the counter and buy medicine there without seeing a doctor. Taiwan sorts medicines into three groups: prescription drugs (處方藥), which need a doctor's prescription (處方箋); pharmacist-advised drugs (指示藥); and over-the-counter drugs (成藥). If a clinic gives you a prescription instead of the medicine itself, take it with your 健保卡 to a pharmacy with a 健保特約藥局 sign. When you're ill, pharmacists and family will often tell you to drink 溫開水 and avoid 冰的.

units.can_do_en: I can send a parcel abroad, choose between air and sea mail after asking how long and how much, and ask where the ATM is and whether my card costs a fee.

grammar.note_en: 這個包裹我要寄到美國: 到 + place right after the verb says where the parcel will end up. Nothing goes between 寄 and 到. You'll say it at every post office counter: 寄到台北, 寄到日本.
The clerk asks 你要寄空運還是海運？: 還是 offers two choices, so the question needs no 嗎. Answer with the one you pick: 寄空運.
Opening the account is already known; 是上個月在這裡開的 puts the focus on when and where it happened. 是 goes before the detail, 的 at the end, and there is no 了.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep ㄢ and ㄤ apart: 單子 ㄉㄢ ˙ㄗ and 便宜 ㄆㄧㄢˊ ㄧˊ end with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth; 帳戶 ㄓㄤˋ ㄏㄨˋ, 銀行 ㄧㄣˊ ㄏㄤˊ and 這張 ㄓㄜˋ ㄓㄤ end open, with the back of the tongue raised ("ahng"). Tone pair 2+2 (two rises): 郵局 ㄧㄡˊ ㄐㄩˊ and 銀行 ㄧㄣˊ ㄏㄤˊ. Let both syllables rise; don't let the second one fall. In 郵局 the ㄐㄩˊ needs rounded lips with the tongue held for ㄧ. 一共 is written ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ but said ㄧˊ ㄍㄨㄥˋ, and 不用 is said ㄅㄨˊ ㄩㄥˋ.

Why does he choose airmail?

The clerk says sea mail is not possible.

He pays the fee at the counter.

speaking.prompt_en: You're at a post office in Pingtung, sending a parcel home. Say where it's going, ask how long air and sea mail take and what they cost, pick one, say what's inside, and then ask whether there's an ATM.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你在屏東的郵局寄包裹回你的國家。請說要寄到哪裡，問空運跟海運要多久、多少錢，選一個，說裡面是什麼東西，再問郵局有沒有提款機。
checklist_en: said where the parcel goes with 寄到 + place
asked or answered an either/or question with 還是 (空運還是海運)
asked 需要多久？ and 多少錢？
asked 有提款機嗎？ or said 我想領錢
kept ㄢ (單子) and ㄤ (帳戶, 銀行) apart, and let both syllables of 郵局 rise

writing.prompt_en: Write a short LINE message (3–5 sentences) to a friend: you went to the post office today, what you sent and where to, whether you chose air or sea mail and why, and what you did afterwards.
writing.prompt_zh: 請寫一個短短的LINE訊息給朋友：你今天去郵局寄了什麼、寄到哪裡、寄空運還是海運、為什麼，還有寄好了以後做了什麼。

units.culture_en: Taiwan's post office, Chunghwa Post (中華郵政), also runs a savings bank: at the same counters you can mail a parcel or open an account (帳戶), and post offices, even in small towns, have ATMs (提款機). Taking cash out with another bank's card (跨行提款) costs a small fee (手續費). Outside a post office you'll see two mailboxes: the green one is for ordinary mail within Taiwan, and the red one is for prompt delivery (限時) and airmail.

units.can_do_en: I can call a friend back, explain why I missed the call, ask them to repeat what I didn't catch, and agree on a time and place to meet, with the address sent on LINE.

grammar.note_en: Mark explains the missed calls with 我剛剛在騎車: 在 + verb for an action that was going on at that moment. It is the usual excuse on the phone: 我剛剛在上課 / 在洗澡，沒聽到。

Two verb + result pairs: 我沒聽清楚 'I didn't hear it clearly', the phrase for asking someone to repeat on a bad line, and 加好了 'done adding you'. When the result didn't happen, the negative is 沒 + verb + result.
我一掛電話就傳地址給你: 一 before the first verb and 就 before the second, 'as soon as I hang up, I'll send you the address'. In 一掛 the 一 is said ㄧˊ, because 掛 is a fourth tone.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep ㄣ and ㄥ apart. 小心 ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄒㄧㄣ and 怎麼 ㄗㄣˇ ˙ㄇㄜ close with the tongue tip; 星期 ㄒㄧㄥ ㄑㄧˊ, 聽到 ㄊㄧㄥ ㄉㄠˋ, 清楚 ㄑㄧㄥ ㄔㄨˇ and 等一下 ㄉㄥˇ ㄧ ㄒㄧㄚˋ close with the back of the tongue (compare 信 ㄒㄧㄣˋ / 姓 ㄒㄧㄥˋ). Many Taiwan speakers say ㄧㄥ like ㄧㄣ, so 聽 can sound like ㄊㄧㄣ: understand it, but produce ㄧㄥ. Tone pair 4+4: 電話, 見面 and 外面 are two high falls in a row; start the second one high again instead of letting it trail off. 一 changes before a fourth tone: 一掛 and 一次 are written ㄧ but said ㄧˊ.

speaking.prompt_en: A Taiwanese friend called you twice while you were busy. Call back: open with 喂 and say who you are, ask if they called, say what you were doing, ask them to repeat something you didn't catch, and agree on a time and place to meet. Ask them to send the address on LINE.
speaking.prompt_zh: 朋友打給你兩次，你都沒接。請你打給他：先說「喂」和你是誰，問他剛剛有沒有打給你，說你剛剛在做什麼。有一句話沒聽清楚，請他再說一次。最後約時間和地方，請他用LINE傳地址給你。
checklist_en: opened with 喂 and said who you are (我是……)
asked 你剛剛有打給我嗎？
said what you were doing with 在 + verb (我剛剛在……)
asked them to repeat: 我沒聽清楚，你可以再說一次嗎？
agreed on a time and place and asked them to 用LINE傳地址給我
kept ㄣ (小心) and ㄥ (聽到, 清楚) apart

writing.prompt_en: A friend called while you were busy and you missed it. Write a short LINE message (3–5 sentences): say sorry, say what you were doing, ask what they need, and say when you'll call back.
writing.prompt_zh: 朋友打給你的時候，你在忙，沒接到。請寫一個短短的LINE訊息：說不好意思，說你剛剛在做什麼，問他有什麼事，再說你什麼時候會打給他。
writing.model_zh: 阿傑，不好意思，你剛剛打給我的時候，我在上課，沒聽到。你找我有什麼事嗎？我五點下課，一下課就打給你。如果很急，可以先傳LINE給我喔！

units.culture_en: LINE is the messaging app most people in Taiwan use: friends, families, classmates and co-workers keep in touch in LINE chats and groups, many shops and clinics have LINE accounts, and many people make free voice and video calls on it instead of dialling. To add someone, you scan their QR code or search for their LINE ID or phone number, if their settings allow it. Stickers (貼圖) are a big part of the conversation; some are free and many are sold. Once your message has been read, LINE shows 已讀 ('read') next to it, and 已讀不回 ('read, no reply') is an everyday complaint about someone who saw your message and didn't answer. Taiwan mobile numbers have ten digits and start with 09 (09xx-xxx-xxx), and people usually read them out in those groups. Calls are answered with 喂？ The MOE dictionary writes it ㄨㄟˋ, but on the phone it is often said with a rise, ㄨㄟˊ, which is how the TBCL word list gives it.

units.can_do_en: I can view a room for rent, ask about the rent, the deposit and the bills, ask whether it's noisy and where to park, and ask for a lower price.

grammar.note_en: The landlady greets Mark with 你就是昨天打電話來的馬克喔？: the clause 昨天打電話來 + 的 comes before 馬克, where English says 'Mark, who called yesterday'. Rooms get described the same way: 我昨天看的套房 'the studio I saw yesterday'.
阿芳 sums up the room with 又大又乾淨 'both big and clean', with no 很 after 又. The two qualities point the same way, so it works for praise and for complaints alike: 又小又貴.

The landlady will 帶你們上去 'take you up' to the third floor, and Mark asks when he can 搬進來 'move in'. They are standing in the room, so it is 來 (toward the speaker); in his message from somewhere else Mark writes 搬進去.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep ㄣ and ㄥ apart. ㄣ ends with the tongue tip on the gum ridge: 押金 ㄧㄚ ㄐㄧㄣ, 新 ㄒㄧㄣ, 陳 ㄔㄣˊ. ㄥ ends with the back of the tongue raised and the tip down: 乾淨 ㄍㄢ ㄐㄧㄥˋ, 姓 ㄒㄧㄥˋ, 冷氣 ㄌㄥˇ ㄑㄧˋ, 停 ㄊㄧㄥˊ. Many Taiwan speakers merge ㄧㄥ into ㄧㄣ, so 姓陳 can sound like 信陳; understand it, but produce the difference. Tone pair 2+1 (rise, then stay high and level): 房東, 房租, 房間, 騎車. Start the rise low enough that the second syllable can sit level at the top.

units.culture_en: Rental listings in Taiwan say whether a room is a 套房, with its own bathroom, or a 雅房, which shares a bathroom with other tenants. A deposit (押金) of two months' rent is the usual deal, and the Rental Housing Market Development and Regulation Act (租賃住宅市場發展及管理條例) does not allow more than two months' rent as a deposit; you get it back when you move out, minus anything you still owe. In a rented room, electricity is often charged by the 度 (one kilowatt-hour) on the room's own meter, so ask how much one 度 costs before you sign. You will also see red 吉屋出租 'house for rent' signs: 吉屋 'lucky house' is the polite way to say 空屋 'empty house'.

units.can_do_en: I can talk about a coming typhoon, change a weekend plan because of the weather and say why, and understand what a neighbour tells me to get ready.

vocab.en: typhoon; 颱風天 a typhoon day
what should we do? what about...?
it's a pity, what a shame
to prepare, to get ready; 準備好 all ready
power cut; the power goes off (停水 the water goes off)
to close, to shut; to turn off; 關好 shut properly
work and classes are called off (for a typhoon)

grammar.note_en: Mark names the problem and puts 怎麼辦 at the end: 我們去墾丁的計畫怎麼辦？ 'What about our Kenting plan?' After a noun, 怎麼辦 asks what will happen to that thing now.
陳阿姨 explains why to buy so much water: 因為 + the reason (water and power can go off), 所以 + the result (get ready beforehand). The reason comes first, as it usually does in Chinese.
阿傑 says 颱風天去墾丁太危險了: 太 + adjective + 了 for 'too...', more than is OK. Mark's 好可惜喔 is different: there 好 just means 'so, really'.

pronunciation.note_en: Keep ㄣ (tongue tip) and ㄥ (back of the tongue) apart: 墾丁 ㄎㄣˇ ㄉㄧㄥ has both, and so do 新聞 ㄒㄧㄣ ㄨㄣˊ vs 停電 ㄊㄧㄥˊ ㄉㄧㄢˋ and 小心 ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄒㄧㄣ vs 青菜 ㄑㄧㄥ ㄘㄞˋ. Many Taiwan speakers merge ㄧㄥ into ㄧㄣ and say 風 like 'fong'; understand it, but produce the standard. Tone pair 2+1 (rise, then high and level): 颱風, 明天, 屏東, 停班. Two Taiwan readings to keep: 危險 ㄨㄟˊ ㄒㄧㄢˇ and 可惜 ㄎㄜˇ ㄒㄧˊ, both with a T2. In 好可惜 the first 好 is said ㄏㄠˊ (3+3), 晚一點 is said with 一 as ㄧˋ, and 不要 is said ㄅㄨˊ ㄧㄠˋ.

speaking.prompt_en: A typhoon is on its way to Pingtung. Call a friend you had weekend plans with: say when the typhoon is coming, say you can't go and why, suggest a new time, and remind your friend what to get ready.
speaking.prompt_zh: 颱風要來屏東了。請打電話跟朋友說：颱風什麼時候來、你們週末為什麼不能去玩了、什麼時候再去，還有要先準備什麼。
checklist_en: said when the typhoon is coming (颱風明天就要來了)
gave the reason with 因為……所以……
used 太……了 (太危險了)
suggested a new time (我們改下個週末再去吧)
named two things to get ready (水、泡麵……)
kept ㄣ (新聞, 墾) and ㄥ (颱風, 停電, 丁) apart

writing.prompt_en: A typhoon is coming. Write a short LINE message (3–5 sentences) to a friend: say the typhoon is coming, say your Saturday trip is off and why, suggest a new time, and remind your friend to get ready.
writing.prompt_zh: 颱風要來了。請寫一個短短的LINE訊息給朋友：說颱風要來了、你們星期六為什麼不能去玩了、改什麼時候去，還有提醒朋友要先準備。
writing.model_zh: 小美，你有看新聞嗎？颱風明天晚上就要來了。因為颱風天出去玩太危險了，所以我們星期六不要去墾丁了。我們改下個週末再去，好不好？今天記得先去超市買水和泡麵喔！

units.culture_en: Typhoon warnings in Taiwan, first for the sea and then for land (海上 / 陸上颱風警報), come from the Central Weather Administration (中央氣象署). When a typhoon is on its way, each city or county government decides whether work and classes stop the next day (停班停課), following national rules from the Directorate-General of Personnel Administration (行政院人事行政總處), whose website lists every area's decision; the announcement usually comes the evening before. People call the day off a 颱風假 'typhoon day off'. Before a typhoon, many people stock up on drinking water, instant noodles and vegetables and charge their phones, because the water or the power can go off for a while.
